thread.title_full: As Roofs Across Jennings Reach the End of Their Lifespan, Homeowners Ask: What Does a New Roof Really Cost?

author: Newport Daily Express
title: As Roofs Across Jennings Reach the End of Their Lifespan, Homeowners Ask: What Does a New Roof Really Cost?
text:
roof installation - Daigle Roofing and Construction Daigle Roofing and Construction explains the planning factors behind new roof installation pricing in Southern Louisiana JENNINGS, La. - Many homes throughout Jennings and Southern Louisiana were roofed within a similar timeframe, and as those roofs approach 20 to 25 years old, homeowners are increasingly asking a practical question: what should they expect to pay for a full roof replacement? Daigle Roofing and Construction says the answer requires looking at the home itself, not just a general price per square foot.
Roof size is typically the first factor contractors evaluate, since larger roofs require more material and labor regardless of other variables. But size alone does not determine cost. The roofing material selected has a major impact on price, with standard asphalt shingles generally the most budget-friendly option, while metal roofing, architectural shingles and tile systems carry higher material and installation costs but often come with longer expected lifespans.
Whether the old roof needs to be torn off before installation is another major cost factor. In some cases, new shingles can be installed over a single existing layer if the decking is sound, though this is not always advisable for long-term performance. When a full tear-off is required, particularly on older homes with multiple layers of roofing material, labor and disposal costs increase accordingly.
The pitch, or steepness, of a roof also plays a role in installation pricing. Steeper roofs require additional safety equipment and more time to install safely, which is reflected in labor costs. Homes with complex rooflines, multiple valleys, or dormers typically cost more to reroof than homes with simple, single-slope designs, even when the total square footage is similar.
Decking condition is often the biggest unknown until a contractor removes the old roofing material. If the plywood or wood decking underneath has been damaged by long-term moisture exposure, it must be repaired or replaced before new roofing can be installed, which adds to both material and labor costs. This is one of the most common reasons a final installation price can differ from an initial estimate.
Underlayment, the moisture barrier installed beneath the roofing material, is another consideration. Basic felt underlayment is less expensive than synthetic or high-performance underlayment options, but the region's humidity and storm exposure lead many homeowners in Southern Louisiana to invest in more durable underlayment as part of a long-term roofing strategy.
"When someone's roof is nearing the end of its life, the goal is to help them plan for it instead of reacting to an emergency," said the owner of Daigle Roofing and Construction. "Once we look at the size, the material choice and the condition of the decking, the homeowner has a much clearer picture of what to expect."
Taken together, these factors mean that new roof installation costs in Southern Louisiana can vary substantially from one home to the next, even among houses of similar size. A straightforward asphalt shingle installation on a simple roofline with sound decking will typically cost less than a metal roof installation requiring a full tear-off and decking repairs on a steep, multi-level home.
Daigle Roofing and Construction recommends that homeowners with roofs older than 15 to 20 years begin planning for replacement before problems arise, rather than waiting for a leak to force an urgent decision. An early inspection allows a contractor to assess decking condition, measure the roof accurately, and provide a detailed estimate that reflects the home's specific characteristics rather than a generic average.
The company also encourages homeowners to request itemized estimates that separate tear-off, decking repair, underlayment, material and labor costs, which allows for more accurate comparisons between contractors and reduces the likelihood of unexpected charges once installation begins.
